name: Q1 Visa (family of Chinese citizens or permanent residents, long-term)

requirement_groups.name: Spouse, minor child, or qualifying relative

requirements.blocker_text: Covers spouses, minor children, and (in a narrower category) elderly relatives over 60 with no other family abroad, of Chinese citizens or foreigners holding Chinese permanent residence, for intended stays exceeding 180 days.
The sponsoring family member must be a Chinese citizen or hold Chinese permanent residence (the Five-Star Card) -- family of ordinary foreign workers or students uses the separate S visa instead.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate, birth certificate, or documentation proving the qualifying family relationship
Sponsor's Chinese ID/household registration or Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card

outcome.duration_length: up to 5 years multiple-entry, converted to a Residence Permit for Family Reunion after arrival

sources.title: China Neighbor -- China Visa Types: Complete Guide for Foreigners (2026), describing Q1/Q2 eligibility

notes: The elderly-relative qualifying path (over 60, no direct relatives abroad, 5 years' continuous residence already in China, stable housing and income) is a genuinely distinctive category not seen in comparable form in most other countries in this dataset -- it describes a narrow reverse-dependency case (an elderly person already established in China with no remaining family ties abroad) rather than a fresh family-reunion application, confirmed via the English Wikipedia's reproduction of China's family-based permanent-residence provisions (itself citing official Chinese-language sources). pr_after_months (60) reflects the general permanent-residence spouse track requiring 5 years of marriage plus 5 years of physical residence at 9+ months/year -- see cn_permanent_residence for the full detail; this route (Q1) is the entry visa/residence-permit status a spouse holds during that qualifying period, not the permanent-residence grant itself. HONEST SOURCING GAP: as with the other 'visit-adjacent' entry visas in this build, no direct nia.gov.cn category page was fetched -- this rests on a cross-referenced tier-3 guide, consistent with the general pattern noted across this build of China's operational visa mechanics being harder to source at tier-1 than this dataset's other countries.
